exposure: pre-admission surgeries/procedures (caesarean section, vaginal delivery, laparotomy for ectopic pregnancy)
clinical characteristics (Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, post-partum haemorrhage, intra-uterine foetal death)
outcome: transfer to non-obstetric or multi-specialty care
cohort: The study included 525 obstetric patients admitted to the ICU at the Government Lalla Ded Hospital, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, India, between March 2022 and February 2023.
finding: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and post-partum haemorrhage were the most common maternal presentations in obstetric ICUs, with patients having heart disease, requiring invasive mechanical ventilation or inotropic support, or admitted after intra-uterine foetal death or laparotomy for ectopic pregnancy showing increased mortality risk.
mod_finding: Only a small percentage (2% of CS and 1% of VD) of patients needed ICU admission, and admission after vaginal delivery was associated with a decreased mortality risk in the ICU.
